description: Fixed 15-drug panel for the ESBL/MDR E. coli UTI MVP scope. Each drug is mapped either directly onto reaction(s) of a genome-scale metabolic model (simulation_mode='direct') or flagged as outside metabolic-model scope (simulation_mode='non_metabolic') when its target (ribosome, DNA gyrase, RNA polymerase, or a non-metabolic activation pathway) is not represented as a gene/reaction in the reconstruction. Non-metabolic drugs still appear in the panel and get literature/rule-based reasoning, but no FBA growth curve.

drugs.notes: First committed step of peptidoglycan precursor synthesis; essential in silico.
Model carries an isozyme (folM/b1606) with weak promiscuous activity, mirroring real trimethoprim biology where FolM gives low-level, clinically minor backup activity.
Sequential blockade partner for trimethoprim in the same pathway (co-trimoxazole); classic literature-validated synergy pair, useful as an internal sanity check for the Bliss/FIC math.

Beta-lactam subclasses share this reaction set in the model (GEMs do not resolve PBP-binding-affinity differences); subclasses are differentiated mainly through the resistance overlay (beta-lactamase hydrolysis profiles), not the baseline target.
Tazobactam's beta-lactamase inhibition is represented in the resistance overlay (it blunts, not eliminates, ESBL hydrolysis of the partner drug).
Prototypical ESBL substrate; strongly hydrolysed by CTX-M-15 in the resistance overlay.
ESBL substrate, hydrolysed similarly to ceftriaxone in the resistance overlay.
Stable to ESBL hydrolysis in the overlay; only carbapenemases (e.g. KPC) degrade it.
More ESBL/porin-loss susceptible than meropenem in practice; overlay gives it partial (not full) protection against ESBL.

Colistin's real target is mature LPS on the outer membrane, not LpxC catalysis directly; using the committed, rate-limiting step of lipid A biosynthesis as a proxy captures the same essential-pathway dependency and gives a graded dose-response, but is a simplification worth flagging. Gene/reaction corrected after verification against the loaded model: an earlier version of this panel used b0180 and its 3-hydroxyacyl-ACP dehydratase reactions (fabZ, fatty acid synthesis) by mistake -- similar-sounding reaction name, wrong enzyme. b0096/UHGADA (UDP-3-O-acetylglucosamine deacetylase) is confirmed here to be single-gene, single-reaction, and essential (full knockout drives growth to exactly zero), matching LpxC's known biology.

drugs.target_enzyme: Nitroreductases (activate prodrug to multi-target reactive intermediates)
drugs.pathway: not represented as a discrete metabolic reaction in this reconstruction
drugs.notes: Verified directly against the loaded model rather than assumed: nfsB is present (gene b0578), but the only reactions it carries in iJO1366 are DHPTDNR/DHPTDNRN (dihydropteridine reductase, a documented NfsB moonlighting activity unrelated to nitrofuran chemistry) -- no nitrofuran-reduction reaction exists anywhere in the model (checked by keyword search over all reaction names). So even though the gene is technically present, the prodrug-activation chemistry nitrofurantoin depends on is genuinely absent, and it damages ribosomes/DNA/multiple enzymes once activated regardless -- multi-target mechanisms a stoichiometric GEM cannot represent either way. nfsA's locus tag could not be independently confirmed against a live database from this environment (no network access) and is left unspecified rather than guessed.

DNA gyrase is not a metabolic enzyme. Verified structurally rather than by trusting a specific locus tag: a keyword search over every reaction name in the loaded model for DNA/RNA-polymerase/ribosome/translation/replication/gyrase/topoisomerase terms returns zero matches -- this reconstruction contains no representation of DNA replication machinery at all, consistent with the standard scope of genome-scale *metabolic* models (see README).

drugs.target_gene: gyrA/gyrB and parC/parE (DNA gyrase and topoisomerase IV)
drugs.notes: Same target class as ciprofloxacin; confirmed absent from the model by the same structural keyword search (see ciprofloxacin notes).

drugs.target_gene: 16S rRNA decoding site (rrsA-rrsH) and 30S ribosomal proteins
drugs.target_enzyme: 30S ribosomal subunit (mistranslation via 16S rRNA A-site binding)
drugs.notes: Aminoglycosides bind the 16S rRNA decoding site, not a specific ribosomal protein; rRNA genes and ribosomal proteins are both absent from the model's reaction network (confirmed by the same structural keyword search noted for ciprofloxacin -- translation is represented only as a lumped biomass precursor demand, not as an explicit ribosome mechanism).
